sample_review.rationale: The final sample found three blocks whose citations did not fully support their shape, relational, temporal, change, and generation predicates.

revisions.title: First hypothesis: the One without additions
revisions.body: The first hypothesis is tested by asking what unity excludes. Because the One cannot be many, it has neither parts nor whole; that rules out straight or round shape, whose definitions presume parts. The argument then denies alteration, rotation, locomotion, and rest: change would alter the One, rotation requires parts, locomotion requires a place, and rest requires being somewhere. These are conditional consequences of the hypothesis, not a portrait outside the exercise.

revisions.title: First hypothesis: even sameness disappears
revisions.body: The serial denial now reaches relation. The One is neither the same nor different from itself or another; neither like nor unlike; and neither equal, greater, nor less. Because these predicates require sameness, measures, or temporal comparison, the argument also denies older, younger, same age, and being in time. Hear the sequence as conditional elimination under the hypothesis, not as a positive description.

revisions.title: If the One is not
revisions.body: The negative hypothesis is treated as a qualified proposition, not simple erasure. The non-existent One must still be known and different from the Others, and must participate in being for the sentence ‘the One is not’ to be true. From that tension it is both moving and at rest: its movement is change from being to not-being, not locomotion or rotation, so it both alters and does not alter.
